title: Rakazo vs LobeHub — two different shapes of agent platform
source: Facts read from both live systems on ZBOX. Rakazo: apps/*, packages/contracts/src/ids.ts, contracts/rpc.ts, builtin-tools.ts, docker ps, rakazo-postgres-1. LobeHub: zervi-lobe-postgres17 (the LIVE db — 211 agents, updated 2026-10-17; zervi-lobe-postgres holds a stale 99-agent August snapshot), docker ps, /opt/zervi/lobehub/docker-compose.yml.
thesis: They are not the same product at different maturity — they are different shapes. LobeHub is an agent PLATFORM: many agents, one shared conversation, tools attached per agent as configuration. Rakazo is an agent WORKSPACE: each assistant gets its own Linux computer and its own single thread, so the agent can drive a desktop, not just call APIs.

rakazo: A photographed Thai invoice → read it, do arithmetic, produce a PDF (proven: returned DO-2569-0042)
Shell, files, browser, screen — the work that is not an API call
One assistant per employee, with a persistent desktop and credentials
Thai UI end to end, employee-shaped navigation
lobe: 211 specialists, each with its own persona, model and knowledge — a searchable catalogue
Knowledge bases with vector retrieval (89 KBs, 559 links)
Sharing: workspaces, visibility, groups, market — Rakazo has none of this
Topics: many separate conversations per agent, which is what people expect of chat

theOneLine: LobeHub answers questions; Rakazo does jobs. Neither is a better version of the other.
